current.text: Taylor Jenkins is the new head coach. Doc Rivers is no longer the coach.
Jenkins is expected to push offensive rebounding, a pressure defense that forces turnovers, and a faster transition game.
Jenkins probably runs a tighter ship than the previous coach.
It is unclear whether Jenkins will give Kel'el Ware a fantasy-friendly role or focus on winning.
Giannis Antetokounmpo was traded to Miami. Milwaukee lost his 33% usage and Bobby Portis's shots, so a lot of shots and touches are open.
Tyler Herro, Ryan Rollins and Kevin Porter Jr. will compete for shot creation.
Rollins and Herro are expected to lead the offense. Herro's role is set. Porter's role is in question.
The guard group is very crowded: Herro, Rollins, Porter, Kasparas Jakucionis, Brayden Burries, Gary Trent Jr., AJ Green and Yuta Watanabe.
The guards ahead of rookie Brayden Burries limit his immediate impact.
The roster has 17 players, so at least two must go. It is heavy on small shooting guards and short on wings.
Power forward is the weakest position, arguably the weakest group in the league. The team will likely start a center at the four.
Projected starters are Rollins, Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware and Myles Turner. Turner and Ware can play together.
Experts cannot yet tell how minutes will be split, so the rotation is unclear.
The team is expected to be bad. Its win total is 26.5, 28th of 30. Justin expects about 33 wins.
Milwaukee does not own its draft pick and does not see this as a long-term rebuild, so it has no reason to tank.
More trades are possible after the Giannis deal, and the team may get worse.
The schedule gives no edge either way. Back-to-backs and fantasy playoff games are both near the league middle.

note: Giannis is gone, which frees a lot of usage. Most of it should go to Ryan Rollins and Tyler Herro, and the frontcourt pair of Kel'el Ware and Myles Turner gains too, with a center likely starting at power forward. The guard group is crowded, so bench guards like Porter, Jakucionis, Burries, Green and Trent risk small or uneven minutes, but the team has no reason to tank, so late-season shutdown risk is low. Early on, watch how Taylor Jenkins splits minutes in the backcourt, how he uses Ware, and which two players get cut or traded.
